answer: Before a violet stranger casts its first vote, its sponsor posts a vouch of 30,000 POA into escrow behind a velvet curtain: nothing is released until the invitee clears ten honest rounds. If the invitee later fails an umber proof-of-personhood check, half the vouch is burned and the rest frozen for a season, so every fake identity drains capital from the account that invited it - the loss compounds per duplicate, while honest referrals pay out in full.
